correctness.rationale: With t=beta*z, the conditional Poisson generating function gives survival (1-exp(-lambda*Q))/(1-exp(-lambda)) and hazard beta*lambda*f/expm1(lambda*Q). Using Q'=-f and f'/f=(alpha-1)/t-1, direct logarithmic differentiation gives (f/Q)[V(lambda*Q)-1-m']; the sign is unchanged on changing from t to z. The integral m=integral_0^infinity exp(-y)(1+y/t)^(alpha-1)dy has strictly negative derivative for alpha>1, zero for alpha=1, and strictly positive derivative for alpha<1. Differentiation is dominated on compact positive t intervals. For alpha>=1, V>1 gives strict increase. Otherwise V is strictly increasing onto (1,infinity), so its inverse defines the unique pointwise intensity at derivative zero. Put a=1-alpha: at zero m~Gamma(alpha)t^a, and m'=-1+m(1+a/t)~a*Gamma(alpha)t^(-alpha). At infinity t^2*m'=a*integral exp(-y)y(1+y/t)^(-a-1)dy -> a, and Q~f. Since V(u)-1~u/2 at zero and V(u)~u at infinity, the age-dependent critical intensity diverges at both endpoints. It is continuous and positive inside, so attains a positive finite minimum. Below it the derivative is everywhere negative; at equality it is nonpositive with no constant interval by analyticity and the negative endpoint signs. Above it there is a positive derivative at a minimizing age and negative derivatives on both sides sufficiently far away. Minimizing and maximizing on intervals bracketed by the derivative signs gives an interior minimum and a later maximum; no uniqueness follows or is claimed. Replay python3 -B /workspace/reproductions/4.py uses half-integer survival formulas and finite differences (12 sign checks, illustrative half-shape crossing about 1.65543269); neither that grid nor the frozen script certifies a global minimum.
